title: Discuss intentions, predictions and future milestones
lessons:
## Your goal
Explain a realistic plan, distinguish a firm arrangement from a prediction, understand deadlines, and say what will already be complete before a later step. You will not predict exam success from hours studied. Future language helps organize action; it does not make an uncertain outcome certain.

## Prerequisites and entry check
Retrieve present aller: `je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, elles vont` — I go/am going, you go… . You also need infinitives, time expressions, passé composé participles and Chapter 12 earlier/later relationships. Say one present routine and one completed action. Then say `Demain, je vais appeler le centre.` — Tomorrow I am going to call the centre. If aller is uncertain, practise it before adding the infinitive.

## 1. Futur proche: a plan connected to now
Use present aller plus an infinitive: `Nous allons visiter les locaux.` — We are going to visit the premises. The second verb stays infinitive; do not say nous allons visitons. Negate the conjugated part: `Je ne vais pas accepter tout de suite.` — I am not going to accept immediately. Questions can use intonation or est-ce que: `Est-ce que vous allez participer ?` — Are you going to take part? With a reflexive verb, place its pronoun before the infinitive: `Je vais me renseigner.` — I am going to get information. Negation: `Je ne vais pas m'inscrire aujourd'hui.` — I am not going to register today.

Futur proche often presents a present intention or a prediction based on current evidence: `Regarde ces nuages : il va pleuvoir.` — Look at those clouds: it is going to rain. It is not restricted to the next few minutes: `Je vais reprendre mes études l'année prochaine.` — I am going to resume my studies next year. A time expression and context identify when.

## 2. Futur simple: commitments and projections
For most -er and -ir verbs, keep the infinitive; for many -re verbs, remove its final e. Add -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont: `je parlerai, tu parleras, elle parlera, nous parlerons, vous parlerez, ils parleront` — I will speak, you will speak… . `Je finirai ce soir.` — I will finish tonight. `Nous attendrons votre réponse.` — We will wait for your reply. The endings come from one pattern across verb groups.

Frequent irregular stems need retrieval: être → ser-, avoir → aur-, aller → ir-, faire → fer-, venir → viendr-, tenir → tiendr-, pouvoir → pourr-, vouloir → voudr-, devoir → devr-, savoir → saur-, voir → verr-, envoyer → enverr-, recevoir → recevr-. Impersonal forms: `il faudra` — it will be necessary; `il pleuvra` — it will rain. Examples: `Vous recevrez un code.` — You will receive a code. `Je pourrai venir jeudi.` — I will be able to come Thursday. Spelling changes also matter: acheter gives `j'achèterai` — I will buy; appeler gives `j'appellerai` — I will call. Learn a common verb as a chunk rather than guessing every stem.

Futur simple is common in promises, formal information and predictions: `Le bureau ouvrira à neuf heures.` — The office will open at nine. But it is not automatically more distant or more certain than futur proche. Compare `Je vais vous rappeler.` — I am going to call you back, a present intention, and `Je vous rappellerai.` — I will call you back, a commitment. Both can refer to later today. A present form may also describe a fixed arrangement with a clear time: `Je pars lundi.` — I leave Monday. Choose meaning and register, not a rigid distance rule.

## 3. Sequence future steps
After quand, lorsque and dès que, French normally uses a future tense when the clause refers to future time: `Quand j'aurai la réponse, je vous appellerai.` — When I have the answer, I will call you. English uses have here, but French uses aurai. `Dès que le bureau ouvrira, nous entrerons.` — As soon as the office opens, we will enter. Do not confuse temporal quand with conditional si: `Si j'ai le temps, je passerai.` — If I have time, I will stop by. Not si j'aurai in this real-condition pattern; Chapter 14 develops it.

## 4. Futur antérieur: completed before a future point
Use future avoir or être plus a past participle: `J'aurai terminé avant midi.` — I will have finished before noon. `Elle sera rentrée avant notre appel.` — She will have come home before our call. The auxiliary and agreement rules remain those of Chapter 10: `Les invitations que j'aurai envoyées…` — The invitations I will have sent…; `Elles se seront préparées.` — They will have got ready; `Elles se seront parlé.` — They will have spoken to each other. Use the tense only when completion matters: `Quand nous aurons reçu le devis, nous déciderons.` — Once we have received the quotation, we will decide. Receiving must be complete before deciding. A simple future may be enough for an ordinary event; do not make every future sentence complex. Futur antérieur can also express a guess about a past event in advanced use; recognize that possibility, but future milestones are this chapter's production focus.

## 5. Common traps, useful chunks and sound
`J'espère pouvoir venir.` — I hope to be able to come, expresses hope, not a promise. `Sauf imprévu…` — Barring an unforeseen problem… qualifies a commitment. `D'ici vendredi…` — By Friday… marks a deadline. Do not confuse dans deux jours — in two days, with pendant deux jours — for two days. `Je viendrai dans deux jours et je resterai pendant deux jours.` — I will come in two days and stay for two days.

In futur simple, listen for the r before the ending: `nous partirons` — we will leave, versus `nous partons` — we leave. Contrast -ai in `je viendrai` — I will come with -ais in `je viendrais` — I would come; accent variation can reduce the sound difference, so use context. Browser speech is synthetic and cannot represent all real pronunciation or exam conditions. Use normal-speed listening before transcript reveal; if synthesis fails, retry rather than count a text reading as listening.

## 6. Retrieve before revealing
A. Announce a current intention to ask for information. B. Promise to send a file. C. Say that once you have signed, you will pay. D. Explain whether futur proche must mean tomorrow and futur simple next year.

:::answer
A. `Je vais me renseigner.` — I am going to get information. B. `Je vous enverrai le dossier.` — I will send you the file. C. `Quand j'aurai signé, je paierai.` — Once I have signed, I will pay. D. No: both can describe near or distant events. Their viewpoint and context differ, not a fixed number of days. `Je vais déménager l'an prochain.` — I am going to move next year, is entirely natural.
:::

## 7. Four skills and cumulative review
For listening, note deadlines and dependencies in separate columns. Read an announcement and distinguish an announced event from a conditional possibility. Speak using new dates and constraints, then answer a follow-up without a script. Write an organized plan with one contingency, not a string of conjugations. Recycle past experience to justify the plan and comparisons to choose an option. Split the bank into four groups of 25. Within a four-hour session, use roughly 35 minutes recall, 45 listening, 40 reading, 45 speaking, 45 writing and 30 correction. Revisit after one day, three days, seven days and two weeks. Log errors by intention, stem, time connector or completion relationship. If future stems fail, retrieve six useful irregulars in context; if sequence fails, draw the steps before speaking. Self-assessment is not examiner grading.

activities.title: A realistic schedule
activities.prompt: What must happen before the team books the room?
activities.script: Nous allons organiser une journée de formation en février. Cette semaine, je vais demander deux devis. Quand nous aurons comparé les prix et obtenu l'accord de la direction, nous réserverons la salle. Ensuite, nous enverrons les invitations. Pour l'instant, ne promettez pas de date précise aux participants.
options: The team must compare prices and obtain approval.
The training must already be finished.
activities.explanation: Comparison and management approval are prerequisites for booking. Invitations follow the booking; the date is not yet a promise.

activities.title: A weather contingency
activities.prompt: Which plan is conditional rather than guaranteed?
activities.script: Samedi, nous partirons à huit heures. La visite du centre d'interprétation est confirmée pour dix heures. Après le repas, nous allons marcher près du lac si le temps reste sec. En cas de pluie, nous resterons au centre pour un atelier. Je vous enverrai la liste du matériel vendredi.
options: Sending the equipment list on Friday.
The afternoon walk near the lake.
activities.explanation: The walk depends on dry weather. Rain triggers an indoor workshop; the visit and departure are announced arrangements.

activities.title: A reopening notice
activities.prompt: Which statement accurately represents the timeline?
activities.passage: La bibliothèque rouvrira le 6 avril. D'ici cette date, l'équipe aura installé les nouvelles étagères et testé les bornes de prêt. Les ateliers reprendront le 13 avril. Les réservations seront possibles dès la réouverture, mais aucune inscription ne sera acceptée par téléphone avant le 6 avril.
options: Installation and testing should be complete before reopening.
Reservations start only on April thirteenth.
activities.explanation: Futur antérieur presents installation and testing as completed by April sixth. Workshops resume a week later; reservations begin at reopening.

activities.title: A tentative study plan
activities.prompt: What does the writer commit to, rather than guarantee?
activities.passage: Je vais travailler l'écoute chaque jour et enregistrer deux réponses orales par semaine. Dans un mois, je comparerai mes nouvelles productions aux premières. J'espère comprendre plus facilement les annonces, mais je ne peux pas prévoir un résultat officiel. Si l'écoute reste mon point faible, je réduirai le temps consacré aux exercices déjà maîtrisés.
options: An official language score in one month.
Regular practice and a review after one month.
The elimination of all reading practice.
activities.explanation: The commitment is a practice routine plus a review. Better comprehension is a hope, and an official result is explicitly not predicted.

activities.title: Plan a neighbourhood event
activities.prompt: Invent a small neighbourhood event. Explain current intentions, two firm commitments, a task that must be finished before another task, and a bad-weather alternative. At the halfway point, respond to the imagined update: The venue is unavailable until noon. Adjust your plan spontaneously.
activities.model: Nous allons organiser un échange de livres samedi. Je contacterai les bénévoles et Amira apportera les tables. Quand nous aurons reçu l'autorisation, nous publierons l'annonce. Si le temps est mauvais, nous utiliserons la salle commune. La salle n'est libre qu'à midi ? D'accord, nous commencerons à treize heures au lieu de dix heures. Je préviendrai les participants vendredi et nous préparerons les livres chez moi le matin. Ainsi, tout sera prêt quand nous entrerons dans la salle.
rubric: Fulfillment: intentions, commitments, dependency and contingency are present.
Interaction: adjusts to the unavailable morning venue.
Coherence: listeners can follow deadlines and order.
Range/control: future stems, conditional si plus present and future completion are meaningful.
Intelligibility: speaks from keywords with understandable pacing.

activities.title: Send a project update
activities.prompt: Write 100–140 words to volunteers planning an invented event. Give dates or relative deadlines, explain one prerequisite, identify a tentative element and request a reply. Learning task; models illustrate possibilities, not one compulsory answer.
activities.model:
Bonjour à toutes et à tous,
Nous allons préparer notre atelier de réparation pour le samedi 12 décembre. Je confirmerai la salle lundi. Quand nous aurons reçu l'accord du centre, nous publierons l'annonce dans le quartier. D'ici mercredi, j'aurai réuni les outils disponibles. Merci de m'indiquer avant mardi ce que vous pouvez apporter et vos heures de présence. Le nombre de places restera provisoire jusqu'à la confirmation des bénévoles. Si nous sommes trop peu nombreux, nous limiterons les inscriptions plutôt que de réduire la qualité de l'accueil. Je vous enverrai un programme détaillé vendredi. Nous ferons ensuite un court bilan après l'atelier.
Merci pour votre aide,
Lucie
rubric: Fulfillment: updates volunteers, gives deadlines, a dependency and a reply request.
Organization: responsibilities and order are clear.
Range: distinguishes intentions, commitments and tentative elements.
Control: future forms, time connectors and si pattern are accurate.
Register: helpful, collaborative email within the suggested length.
